indicators.note: after places the Greek letter behind the abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A shopper picks out a fine Greek cheese, the national character showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white brined cheese from Greece, so it is an example of a cheese.

indicators.note: electrifying suggests a jolt that throws things about, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to wire live cables onto a fence to keep intruders out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a fence is only one example of the answer, as in a show-jumping course.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing and show jumping a fence is a barrier the horse must clear, an example of a hindrance.

parts.note: to put on a show is to feign, or sham
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone dons a piece of clothing to pass as a fake doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack is someone who claims healing powers without medical training, which loosely describes a tribal medicine man.

clue.text: Lucky it being nothing more than a grand

parts.note: just means only, nothing more than
swell is an old-fashioned word for grand or excellent

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a mere thousand pounds was a fortunate sum to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a grand' looks like a thousand pounds, but it splits into the article plus an old-fashioned word for splendid. 'it being' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is just as well means it is fortunate that things turned out that way.

clue.text: List by counter where shoes may be repaired

parts.note: a ship that lists heels over to one side
a bar is the counter in a pub

explanation.surface: A catalogue sits beside the shop counter where a cobbler fixes footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel bar is a small shop or kiosk offering quick shoe repairs and key cutting while you wait.

clue.text: Dye head of horse princess raised

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of horse is used
in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Anne is the Princess Royal, the King's sister

explanation.surface: A princess colours the mane of her raised horse with dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown colouring made from a plant, used on hair and skin.

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so a fight between those who run things is cryptically one between runners

explanation.walkthrough: The plain meaning is a long-continuing dispute; the joke reads 'running' as managing.
explanation.definitionFit: A running battle is a fight or argument that carries on over a long period.

indicators.note: round says the search word goes around the area letter

parts.note: to hunt is to search

explanation.surface: Someone combs the neighbourhood around a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place one frequents, and resort can mean a place regularly visited, as in last resort.

clue.text: Male in working party gets treatment

indicators.note: in places the male pronoun inside the rearranged letters
working means the letters of party are worked into a new order

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man at a busy works party is given some medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' makes TRAPY from party; 'in' puts HE inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal or relieve a disorder.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: Someone is genuinely impressed by a well-liked woman's show.
explanation.definitionFit: In fact is used to stress the truth of a statement, just like really or actually.

clue.text: Gossip involving old maiden? It's not important

indicators.note: involving means the chatter word wraps around the abbreviations

parts.note: to natter is to chat or gossip
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for maiden, an over with no runs

explanation.surface: Chatter about an elderly spinster is dismissed as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: No matter is said to brush something aside as of no consequence.

definitions.meaning: Daphne du Maurier's 1936 novel set in Cornwall
an inn named after a country, and the real ... is a pub on Bodmin Moor

explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn is both a famous novel and the actual old coaching inn in Cornwall that inspired it.

clue.text: Old English instrument to feature in a long jazzy number coming up

indicators.note: the instrument appearing in the rest means it is set inside the other letters
jazzy suggests a lively improvisation, so the letters of a long are rearranged
in a down clue coming up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: sax is short for saxophone

explanation.surface: A saxophone takes the lead in a long, lively jazz number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazzy' signals the anagram of 'a long'; 'coming up' reverses the abbreviation for number, as befits a down clue; 'to feature in' sets the instrument inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Saxon is the language of England before the Norman Conquest, also called Old English.

clue.text: Lose one's temper in card game

definitions.meaning: a children's card game where players call out on matching cards

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden angry outburst and a simple matching game played with cards.

indicators.note: circulating means moving about, so the letters of the previous words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone routinely passes photos of suspects around the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogues' gallery is a police collection of photographs of known criminals.

parts.note: a swine is both a pig and a nasty person, and behind the wheel means driving

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally it is a pig driving; really it is a selfish motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a driver who behaves selfishly, hogging the road and endangering others.

parts.note: Chantilly in France gives its name to a fine bobbin lace
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A shopper finds the price of some French fabric has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a price reduction but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or slash the flesh, making a cut.

clue.text: Staple food that may give South American energy

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A dietary staple supposedly fuels a South American with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, a basic carbohydrate in parts of Southeast Asia.

clue.text: University head's in luck getting tube back

parts.note: chance means luck

indicators.note: back means the letters for tube are read in reverse

parts.note: a roll is a cylinder, like a tube

explanation.surface: A vice-chancellor is fortunate to catch the Underground home.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities the chancellor is the titular ceremonial head of the institution.

clue.text: Man reduced rent for wooden villa

indicators.note: reduced means the word for man is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A man has his rent cut on a timber holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden house with overhanging eaves, typical of Swiss mountains or holiday villages.

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A newcomer begins working alongside a team.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, as in the onset of winter.

clue.text: Heats pan prepared for game bird

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, here meaning the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook warms a pan ready for cooking a game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed bird shot for sport and food.

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to fuse is to melt, as metal does

explanation.surface: Scrap metal is about to be melted down.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is rubbish, things thrown away as scrap.

indicators.note: about means the message word goes around the size letter

parts.note: a fax is a message sent by telephone line
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A note arrives about a big shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is a blue-flowered plant grown for its fibre, used to make linen.

definitions.meaning: a saw is an old saying
the ... of Zurich is a mocking name for Swiss bankers

explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is an aphorism, and Swiss financiers were derided as the gnomes of Zurich by a British politician in 1964.

parts.note: extra means further or additional
ct is the standard abbreviation for carat

explanation.surface: A jeweller takes away one more carat from a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to draw it out or take it away.
